No uncertainty estimate is provided with GPCP 1dd data. However, the errors in monthly mean values from the GPCP monthly product are also relevant for this dataset. Huffman et al (2001) contains some early validation of the data from the Oklahoma mesonet, and states that random errors could be calculated for this product as they are for GPCP monthly data. Bolvin et al (2009) contains further validation with high-latitude gauges.
GPCP v3.2 shows substantial improvements in representing rain occurrence and rain intensity at daily scale.

claims.text: V1.3 algorithm: TMPI in 40N-S (geo-IR threshold matched to SSM/I-SSMIS GPROF rain frequency, rain rate set so each month sums to the GPCP Monthly), leo-IR fill-in, and TOVS/AIRS at high latitudes rescaled to the monthly. V3.3 algorithm: IMERG Final averaged to 0.5° daily, thresholded at 0.24 mm/d in 55N-S; TOVS/AIRS histogram-matched to IMERG at higher latitudes; boundary feathering; days ratio-scaled to the V3.3 Monthly with ratios capped at 0.2-4.0.

evidence.passage: In the latitude band 40°N-S the Threshold-Matched Precipitation Index (TMPI) produces | approximate instantaneous precipitation from the geo-IR Tb with fill-in by rescaled leo-IR | GPI. It is a GPI-type algorithm with locally calibrated Tb threshold and rainrate. … Then a single rainrate for | "raining" geo-IR pixels is computed for each grid box that makes the full month of TMPI sum | to the local GPCP Monthly value. … The computer used to process the GPCP Daily product is Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server | release 6.7 (version 2.6.32-573.7.1.el6.x86_64). The programming languages and software | include: shell scripts to run the processing code; FORTRAN programs to perform most of the | calculations; C programs to generate the outputs; MATLAB to make the diagnostic plots.

No primary sensor data are used in the V3.3 Daily. Then IMERG is used in the latitude band 55°N-S, and TOVS/AIRS is | used at higher latitudes. … The computer used to process the GPCP Daily product is an Oracle Linux Version 8 server. Difference in scope: each route states its own terms. data.gov gives CC0 for NCEI V3.3; GDEX gives CC BY 4.0; CDS uses GPCP and NASA GES DISC product licences; NCEI's use agreement says the data are open with no restrictions; GES DISC/CMR name no licence.
